title: Two weeks with Lil Armstrong and the stranded tour
summary: A stranded two-week southern tour with Lil Armstrong's band, poor crowds, and McRae's ordeal at a roadside stand.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: It seems to me--I remember you telling me this, I don't know whether you formed your band first or after, but I know you went out with Lil Armstrong.
Oh yeah.
You went out with Lil Armstrong; that was the summer of '37, wasn't it?
I just went down with her for I think two weeks, because we got stranded; we didn't have nobody.
You had a big band.
Yeah, we had a big band but McRae was with the band--
Dick Vance.
Dick Vance, Stumpy--
It was a nice band.
It was a nice band but we didn't draw no people. Just didn't draw flys. We got down in Knoxville, Tennessee and didn't have no place to eat.
What was that story about McRae?

That was the darnest thing. None of us had much money, so we finally got some money from someplace, enough to get us back in the car, for gas and everything, and we were coming back through Tennessee and there was

a little stand on the edge of the highway--just a little stand, not in the city, and the man was so happy we stopped there, because he didn't have no business and we bought hot dogs and hamburgers and soda and things like that, and all of a sudden I heard somebody cursing like hell and this guy opened his door to his bathroom and there was McRae on the stool and I never heard so much--this guy was (inaudible), he said, oh my God, this nigger's got his ass on my stool, oh Lord have mercy, what am I going to do. Nigger, get up off, (inaudible) so we all raced back there to see what it was all about and McRae said I can't stop, I can't get up, and he said this nigger has to get up, this nigger had his ass on my stool, oh my God. I swear to god I'll blow your head off. So he said I can't stop; I went and grabbed McRae by the head and pulled him up.
I bet he'll never forget that.
He'll never forget about that. It was an awful thing down there then.
That's all it was, just a couple of weeks?
Just about two weeks.
So in other words it was all on the road down south?
That's all.
She organized the band here in New York?
Yeah, she organized the band here and we just went down. There wasn't that many dates in the two weeks and I'll never forget in Knoxville we only had about twenty people.
